questions.text: Let G be a connected undirected graph of 100 vertices and 300 edges. The weight of a minimum spanning tree of G is 500. When the weight of each edge of G is increased by five, the weight of a minimum spanning tree becomes ________.
questions.solution:
Every spanning tree has 99 edges, so each tree's weight rises by exactly 99 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 495. The same tree stays minimum.

500 + 495 = 995

Answer: 995

questions.text:
Language [latex]L_{1}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{2}[/latex]. Language [latex]L_{3}[/latex] is polynomial time reducible to [latex]L_{2}[/latex], which in turn is polynomial time reducible to language [latex]L_{4}[/latex]. Which of the following is/are true?
I. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
II. if [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] or [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{2} \in P[/latex]
III. [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex], if and only if [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
IV. if [latex]L_{4} \in P[/latex], then [latex]L_{1} \in P[/latex] and [latex]L_{3} \in P[/latex]
questions.solution:
Reductions: [latex]L_1\le L_2[/latex], [latex]L_3\le L_2\le L_4[/latex]. If the target is in P, the source is in P.

- I: [latex]L_4\in P\Rightarrow L_2\in P[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: then [latex]L_1, L_3\in P[/latex] too [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II and III would need reductions in the other direction [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not implied

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text: Assume that a mergesort algorithm in the worst case takes 30 seconds for an input of size 64. Which of the following most closely approximates the maximum input size of a problem that can be solved in 6 minutes?
questions.solution:
Mergesort time [latex]\propto n\log n[/latex]. For n = 64: 64 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 384 units in 30 s.

6 minutes = 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 30 s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 384 = 4608 units.

n = 512: 512 [latex]\times[/latex] 9 = 4608 [latex]\checkmark[/latex]

Answer: 512

questions.text:
Consider the equality [latex]\sum_{i=0}^{n}i^{3}=X[/latex] and the following choices for X
I.[latex] \Theta (n^{4}) [/latex]
II. [latex] \Theta (n^{5}) [/latex]
III. [latex]O (n^{5}) [/latex]
IV. [latex] \Omega (n^{3})[/latex]
The equality above remains correct if X is replaced by
questions.solution:
[latex]\sum_{i=0}^n i^3=\left(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2=\Theta(n^4)[/latex]

A [latex]\Theta(n^4)[/latex] function is also [latex]O(n^5)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(n^3)[/latex], but it is not [latex]\Theta(n^5)[/latex].

Answer: I or III or IV but not II
